study_design: Retrospective case-control comparison of men with prostate cancer, men with other cancers, and control subjects, including pre- and postdiagnosis dietary assessments.
cohort_total_n_excerpt: Food habits of Argentinean men pre- and post-diagnosis of prostate cancer (n = 326) were assessed along with other lifestyle factors. We studied whether any of the behaviors and risk factors for prostate cancer were found in men with other cancers (n = 394), compared with control subjects (n = 629).
reason: The abstract evaluates prostate cancer cases and controls but does not analyze an aggressive, advanced, high-grade, metastatic, or lethal incident prostate cancer endpoint. Postdiagnosis behavior modification is not aggressive incidence. The prostate cancer comparison comprised 326 cases and 629 controls; the separate other-cancer group was not included in that analytic total.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Before diagnosis, both cases reported a greater mean consumption of meats and fats and lower intakes of fruits, green vegetables, cruciferous vegetables, legumes, nuts, seeds, and whole grains than the controls (all p < 0.001).
estimate_classifications.reason: The legumes comparison concerns prostate cancer and other cancer case groups versus controls, with no aggressive prostate cancer subtype. No effect estimate with a 95% CI is reported in the abstract.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Additional lifestyle aspects significantly predominant in cases included a reduced quality of sleep, emotional stress, low physical activity, tobacco smoking, alcohol consumption, living in rural areas, and being exposed to environmental contaminants.
estimate_classifications.reason: Alcohol consumption was compared in the general case groups and controls, without an aggressive prostate cancer endpoint or an abstract-reported OR and 95% CI.
